context: Distinguish 'the collect subprocess failed' from 'the policy was violated'. When returncode is non-zero, emit a distinct diagnostic naming the interpreter and the missing dependency (and exit non-zero as a tooling error), rather than appending to the policy-violation list. Optionally resolve pytest via the project venv explicitly instead of sys.executable, so the script behaves the same however it is launched.
description: _run_pytest_collect() shells out to [sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', ...]. Invoked the documented agent way -- 'uv run --project _project/scripts -- python _project/scripts/timing_policy_check.py --strict' -- sys.executable is the _project/scripts venv, which has neither pytest nor benchbox installed. Every collect subprocess exits 1 with no parseable count, and the script converts that into policy violations: 'Fast lane policy violations: 4' with four 'could not parse collect count' lines. Nothing is actually wrong with the fast lane. Run from the project env instead ('uv run -- python _project/scripts/timing_policy_check.py --strict') the same tree reports 'Fast lane policy violations: 0'. Found during the 2026-07-24 benchmark-runs batch (PRs #1299-#1302); verified pre-existing by stashing all batch changes and reproducing on a clean tree. Real-world cost: an agent following the pre-approved command list sees 4 FAST_LANE_VIOLATIONs, cannot tell them from a genuine cap breach, and may 'fix' a cap that was never exceeded. CI is unaffected because its lint job invokes the script with the project environment.

deferrals.reason: (1) todo verify grades solely on exit code (todo_db.py:1809 'passed = proc.returncode == 0'), ignoring the prose expectation. Rung 1 runs the script under --strict in the broken env; the CORRECT behaviour there is a non-zero exit, because a policy check that never ran must not report success -- otherwise CI goes green on a broken environment. So the rung can only ever report fail. Verified the rung's intent manually instead: 0 FAST_LANE_VIOLATION lines, no 'Fast lane policy violations' summary, exactly 1 FAST_LANE_ENVIRONMENT_ERROR naming the interpreter, exit 1. Verifications are create-time-only so the rung cannot be amended. (2) tests/unit/scripts/test_timing_policy_modes.py is outside only_modify, but its test_emit_fast_count_unparseable_output_fails_closed asserted the exact string 'could not parse' -- the wording this fix deliberately replaces -- so it had to be updated or CI would go red.
deferrals.summary: Verification rung 1 is unsatisfiable as authored, and the fix needs a test file outside only_modify
